subject: Request: Vulnerability governance evidence, scan cadence, and remediation tempo
messages:
From: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@northstarbank.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: security-audits@northstarbank.com
Date: 2027-06-06T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Evidence request — scan cadence, SLA windows, and CVE remediation attestation

Hi Kimberly,

As part of our SIG intake and upcoming SOC 2 evidence refresh, Northstar needs a compact package that outlines Redwood's vulnerability management tempo. Specifically we need:

- Official scan cadence for internal and external code/artifact scans (scheduling and last run).
- SLA windows for CVE remediation by severity (how you classify critical/high/medium and associated timelines).
- A short attestation we can include in our audit binder that commits Redwood to those timelines (or describes compensating controls / escalation paths).

Can you provide a single PDF (or zip) with the policy, an exported remediation matrix for the last 12 months, and any Drive links to evidence by EOD Friday (2027-06-11)? If there are known exceptions for third-party dependencies or managed services, please call those out.

Thanks — we are on a compressed timeline for the auditor.

Elena Ramos
Senior Information Security Manager
Northstar Bank
elena.ramos@northstarbank.com

[Attachment: intake-guidance.pdf (pdf)]

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@northstarbank.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-06T12:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request — scan cadence, SLA windows, and CVE remediation attestation

Hi Elena — thanks for the note and the deadline. We can deliver the package by Friday. High-level answers here while we assemble the artifacts: 

- Scan cadence: internal image/container SAST and dependency scanning (weekly automated, full inventory monthly), external-facing dynamic scans (DAST) weekly for prod domains, and authenticated scans for main services every 2 weeks. Ad-hoc runs after each production deploy.

- Remediation SLAs (Redwood policy v2.1):
  * Critical (CVSS >= 9.0 or actively exploited): mitigation plan within 48 hours; fix or rollback within 7 days; emergency hotfix windows available.
  * High (CVSS 7.0–8.9): scheduled remediation within 30 calendar days.
  * Medium (CVSS 4.0–6.9): remediation within 90 calendar days.
  * Low (CVSS < 4.0): remediation within 180 calendar days or tracked for next maintenance window.

- Exceptions: third-party managed services that are vendor-controlled are documented and mapped (we include compensating controls and detection coverage).

I'll attach the policy draft and a remediation matrix excerpt now; Dev and Product will add timeline evidence and scan exports.

-Kimberly Park
Security Lead, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

[Attachment: redwood-vm-tempo-policy.pdf (pdf)]

From: dev_patel@redwood.com

Date: 2027-06-07T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Evidence request — scan cadence, SLA windows, and CVE remediation attestation

Kimberly / Marissa — forwarding Elena's request. Two quick notes from Eng:

- We will export the scan run CSVs for the last 12 months (container/image and SCA) and a filterable CVE remediation matrix (owner, ticket link, severity, discovery date, fix date, mitigation). ETA for exports: EOD Thursday.

- For criticals we use our emergency rollout playbook (hotpatch or rollback + test verification). I will add the playbook pointer in the artifacts (runbook id: RB-23017).

Also including proposed wording for the attestation paragraph (feel free to edit):

  "Redwood Inference affirms that vulnerabilities classified as Critical are triaged within 48 hours and remediated or mitigated within 7 calendar days; High-severity issues are remediated within 30 calendar days; Medium within 90 days; Low within 180 days. Exceptions are documented and handled via compensating controls and an escalation path involving Security and Product leadership."

-dev

[Attachment: scan-cadence-report-2027Q2.csv (csv)]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@northstarbank.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-09T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Evidence request — scan cadence, SLA windows, and CVE remediation attestation

Elena — attaching the evidence bundle per your ask. Contents below and short notes: 

1) redwood-vm-tempo-policy.pdf — official policy (signed by Security leadership) with classification, SLA table, and exception process.
2) cve-remediation-matrix.xlsx — exported workbook with tickets and timestamps for remediation across the last 12 months; pivot tab by severity included.
3) scan-cadence-report-2027Q2.csv — automated export of scan runs (SAST/SCA/DAST) for quarter.

Key clarifications:
- Our SLA time windows (Critical 7d / High 30d / Medium 90d / Low 180d) are the standard commitment. For any customer-facing systems we also maintain detection controls (WAF, runtime alerts) and documented compensating controls where immediate patching isn't possible.
- Where a fix requires a vendor update (managed third-party), we document expected vendor remediation ETA and hold an exception record with compensating detection and contract escalation.

Links: evidence folder (internal view): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-vm-evidence
HubSpot reference: HS-45902 (evidence package).

Please see the attestation text in the Policy (page 2). If the auditor needs a signed statement on Redwood letterhead, we can generate that same wording with an executive signature; please confirm.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Security Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

[Attachments: cve-remediation-matrix.xlsx (xlsx), scan-cadence-report-2027Q2.csv (csv)]

Marissa / Kimberly — received, and this looks to meet our needs. Two quick asks before we close the intake:

1) Can you produce the same attestation as a single-page PDF on Redwood letterhead for inclusion in our SOC 2 audit binder? If so, we need that signed and uploaded by 2027-06-14.
2) Please highlight (in the matrix) any items where remediation exceeded the SLA and add a short explanation for the delay. The auditor will expect a corrective action note.

If you can confirm both, we can mark this intake done. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Elena
